allies.rationale_text: Systems-thinking helps cultural-dimensions-theory connect local behavior differences to broader coordination patterns and long-term effects.
allies.source_quote: Models are invaluable in systems thinking contexts, helping users gain a big-picture view, recognize patterns, and visualize the dynamics of complex systems.
allies.affinity_rationale: Described as 'essential tools within systems thinking' — models help conceptualize organizations as machines made up of culture and people, tracing cause-and-effect activities within the system.
allies.activation_condition: When cultural dimensions need to be analyzed as systemic interrelationships within organizational or societal contexts rather than as isolated variables

antagonists.rationale_text: Representativeness-heuristic undermines cultural-dimensions-theory by causing users to treat dimension scores as fixed identity labels for individuals rather than probabilistic context clues, collapsing cultural analysis into stereotyping.
antagonists.source_quote: The model fails when cultural dimensions are treated as fixed labels for individuals rather than probabilistic context clues that still need verification in the real relationship.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: From structured tensions — stereotypes replace context-specific interpretation, causing cultural dimension scores to be applied as fixed categories rather than context-dependent analytical tools.
antagonists.activation_condition: When cultural dimension scores are treated as stereotypical predictions rather than probabilistic tools requiring context-specific calibration

structured_tensions.tension_text: Cultural-dimensions-theory conflicts with optionality when broad cultural branching postpones concrete coordination commitments that now need closure.
structured_tensions.source_quote: cultural-dimensions-theory conflicts with optionality (optionality) when broad cultural branching postpones concrete coordination commitments.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Cultural-dimensions-theory conflicts with opportunity-cost when adapting to one norm set hides the outcomes foregone in alternative contexts.
